canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. In the available formulation, interactive segmentation is treated as a task of segmenting objects in an image by actively incorporating user input. The description centers on separating objects with prompts such as points, boxes, or scribbles, and one snippet summarizes it as work that "separates objects by actively integrating user inputs" (Interfacing Foundation Models' Embeddings).

Variants. The only explicit variants concern the form of user input used to guide segmentation, with points, boxes, and scribbles all named. The paper also mentions a unified training setting in which interactive segmentation is trained together with image-text retrieval.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link interactive segmentation to a single measurement instrument, PASCAL VOC, which is recorded as measuring it. The measurement evidence is brief, with one paper stating that "Interactive segmentation performance is preserved in the unified settings."

What it is taken as evidence of. No construct is linked to interactive segmentation in the available relationships, so the papers here do not specify what construct this behavior is taken to indicate.
